clue.text: Loss of cover? A lot of spies about to run

indicators.note: about means around, so the spy agency and the A go round the running word

parts.note: taken as written
the CIA is a whole lot (group) of American spies
to lope is to run with long easy strides

explanation.surface: A coded message about a band of spies losing their cover and fleeing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loss of cover' sounds like blown espionage cover; it means loss of hair. The CIA, America's spy agency, is the 'lot of spies'.
explanation.definitionFit: This medical condition is baldness, the loss of the scalp's natural hair covering.

clue.text: Poet celebrated in Sabadell or Cadiz

indicators.note: in signals that the name sits inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A poet is honoured in two Spanish cities.
explanation.walkthrough: The poet's surname runs across the end of Sabadell, the word or, and the start of Cadiz. Fittingly, Federico Garcia Lorca was a Spanish poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Federico Garcia Lorca is a famous Spanish poet and playwright, an example of a celebrated poet.

clue.text: Las Vegas chip?

parts.note: a chip in Las Vegas suggests a gambling token, but an American chip is the fried potato snack the British call by another name

explanation.surface: A gambling token from a Las Vegas casino.
explanation.definitionFit: What Americans call a chip is the thin fried potato slice sold in bags in Britain.

clue.text: Item of lingerie in lace — I'm so excited

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled by a lacy piece of underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' shuffles the letters of LACE and IMSO; the word 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A camisole is a light sleeveless top worn as underwear, a classic lingerie garment.

clue.text: How hands may be viewed, subject to time constraints

definitions.meaning: the hands of a clock are seen set against its face
working to a deadline, racing the timer

explanation.surface: A view of a watch face while working under pressure of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Clock hands appear against the face; the idiom means racing to finish before time runs out.

clue.text: Religious leader's origin had to be reviewed

parts.note: a bud is the origin or beginning of a flower

indicators.note: reviewed read as re-viewed, looked at afresh, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The beginnings of a religious leader had to be looked at again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be reviewed' rearranges HAD into DHA; the 's after leader is a link meaning is.
explanation.definitionFit: The Buddha, Siddhartha Gautama, is the founder of Buddhism, so a religious leader.

clue.text: Gaudy toy in package youngster's not opening

indicators.note: in places the young animal within the bundle

parts.note: a bale is a large bound package of goods

indicators.note: not opening means without its first letter

parts.note: a cub is a youngster, especially a young animal or Cub Scout

explanation.surface: A cheap shiny toy in a parcel that a child won't unwrap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not opening' strips the C from CUB, leaving UB; 'Gaudy toy' is the definition, not part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A bauble is a showy trinket of little value, a gaudy plaything.

clue.text: What's the point of a code?

definitions.text: What's the point of a code?

parts.words: What's the point of a code?
parts.note: reads as asking why codes exist, but asks which point or mark is a symbol in Morse code

explanation.surface: Someone asking what purpose a code serves.
explanation.definitionFit: In Morse code a short signal written as a small point is one of the two basic symbols.

clue.text: Difficult punishment that's too bad

parts.note: hard means difficult
lines are a school punishment, a sentence written out many times

explanation.surface: A tough penalty that seems excessive.
explanation.walkthrough: LINES are a British school punishment where a pupil copies a sentence many times; 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of sympathy for bad luck, an idiom meaning that's unfortunate.

clue.text: National leader keeping normal routine for now

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the leader goes around the routine

parts.note: PM, the Prime Minister, leads the nation
rote is a fixed routine of habit or repetition

explanation.surface: A prime minister sticking to the usual schedule for the time being.
explanation.walkthrough: Pro tem is short for the Latin pro tempore; the 'National leader' is Britain's Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin pro tempore, shortened, means for the time being, temporarily.

clue.text: True lady misrepresented in this?

indicators.note: misrepresented means shown falsely, so the letters are presented in a different order

explanation.surface: A supposedly faithful woman falsely portrayed in an affair.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a lady not true to her spouse, misrepresenting herself, is committing exactly this.
explanation.definitionFit: Infidelity in marriage is the act a lady untrue to her husband would be engaged in.

clue.text: Well-upholstered, initially comfortable to sit in? It's true

indicators.note: sitting in something means being placed inside it

parts.note: well-upholstered is a jokey way of saying plump or fat

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of comfortable

explanation.surface: Someone praising a well-padded chair as comfortable to sit in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes C from comfortable, which goes inside FAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is true is a certainty, a statement of truth rather than opinion.

clue.text: Only the one document in a queue?

parts.note: single means only one
a file is a document or set of records

explanation.surface: Someone asking if just one document is waiting in line.
explanation.definitionFit: Walking in a line one behind another is the idiom for being in a queue.

clue.text: Pain, say, dealing with euros?

parts.note: pain looks like suffering but is the word for a loaf in the language of a euro-using country

explanation.surface: Suffering caused by handling the euro currency.
explanation.walkthrough: Pain is the French word for bread; France pays in euros.
explanation.definitionFit: Pain is the French language's word for a loaf, the bread of a euro-zone nation.

clue.text: Round Table member: knight occupying network with a great many

indicators.note: occupying means filling, so the knight sits inside the network

parts.note: lace is a network of threads
N is the chess notation for knight
a lot means a great many

explanation.surface: A knight of King Arthur's circle surrounded by many in a network.
explanation.walkthrough: N is knight in chess notation; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Lancelot was one of King Arthur's knights of the Round Table.

clue.text: Country trails winding through Gold Check tod Coast's centre

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Country trails winding through Gold Check tod Coast's centre': 'Check tod' is OCR intrusion (parse is AU + anagram of TRAILS + A, centre of COAST), and the scan crop is illegible, so the printed clue cannot be confirmed
annotationWithheld.clue: Country trails winding through Gold Check tod Coast's centre

clue.text: Woman's range curtailed after setback

indicators.note: a setback here is a turning back, so the shortened range reads backwards
curtailed means having its tail, the last letter, cut off

parts.note: the Andes is a mountain range

explanation.surface: A woman whose range of options has been cut after a setback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtailed' cuts the S off ANDES, giving ANDE; 'after setback' turns that round. The 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Edna is a woman's first name.

clue.text: HQ standpoint is the yardstick

parts.note: a base is a headquarters
a line is a position or standpoint taken on a question

explanation.surface: The headquarters' official view sets the standard.
explanation.definitionFit: A baseline is a reference point for measuring change, a yardstick.

clue.text: When vermouth is kept back, there's wine

parts.note: as can mean when, as in as I left

indicators.note: kept back means held in reverse, so the vermouth reads backwards

parts.note: It is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and It

explanation.surface: Once the vermouth runs out, there is still wine to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gin and It' is gin with Italian vermouth, so IT is vermouth; 'kept back' turns it to TI.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine from Piedmont.

clue.text: Crazy receptacle for displaying a bust?

definitions.meaning: slang for a mad or unbalanced person
read literally, a glass box for showing a sculpted head

explanation.surface: A display cabinet for a sculpted bust described as mad.
explanation.walkthrough: A bust is a sculpture of the head and shoulders, so a box to show one is literally a case for a head; the slang sense is a madman.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a lunatic, and literally a case to hold a sculpted head.

clue.text: Young things going round in the ultimate in suave smart clothes

indicators.note: going round means surrounding, so the young fish enclose the rest

parts.note: fry are young fish
taken as written

indicators.note: the ultimate means the last letter of suave

explanation.surface: Youngsters wearing the latest in elegant smart outfits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the ultimate in' gives E, the last letter of suave; fry are newly hatched fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Finery is elaborate, showy clothing worn for special occasions.

clue.text: It looks like nothing found in a field

definitions.text: It looks like nothing found in a field

parts.words: It looks like nothing found in a field
parts.note: suggests something odd and unearthly in a field, or a shape like a zero flattened into a crop

explanation.surface: A mysterious formation in a field that resembles nothing known.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nothing' is the round letter O, the shape these flattened patterns make in wheat fields.
explanation.definitionFit: These are circular patterns of flattened crops, a ring like the figure zero, in farm fields.

clue.text: Bill for seed?

parts.note: bill looks like an invoice for seed, but is a bird's bill used for pecking seed

explanation.surface: An invoice for a purchase of seed.
explanation.walkthrough: It is also British slang for a magistrate.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird's bill is its horny mouthpart, used by finches to crack seed.

clue.text: Immature, not about to get grant

indicators.note: not means without, so the letter for about is dropped

parts.note: callow means young and inexperienced
C is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: Someone too young to receive a grant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes C (circa) from CALLOW; 'to get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To grant permission is to permit, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Similar character? Change, say, may be linked to love

parts.note: alter means change
eg, for example, is what say means here
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A lookalike character whose change may be tied to love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be linked to' is a link joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A second self, a person's other side, is a character similar to them.

clue.text: When you'd expect to see letter from Greece?

definitions.meaning: estimated time of arrival, when someone is due
the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Wondering when a letter posted from Greece will arrive.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviation for estimated time of arrival, and a Greek letter.

clue.text: Ethics displayed by confused ladies

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Muddled women show their moral principles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'displayed by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideals are moral principles, standards of conduct akin to ethics.

clue.text: Very happy to invite in free-and-easy group of stars

indicators.note: inviting in means taking inside, so happy holds the relaxed word

parts.note: gay in its old sense means very happy, merry
lax means relaxed, free-and-easy

explanation.surface: A cheerful, relaxed host inviting a crowd of celebrities.
explanation.definitionFit: A galaxy is a huge system of stars, like the Milky Way.

clue.text: Don't be seen to collect feathers? (4,4) 23,109 Solution to

parts.note: to keep is to collect and retain, as with stamps
down is soft fine feathers

explanation.surface: Someone hiding while gathering feathers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie low and stay hidden is an idiom for not being seen.
